narratives.name: Platform Risk And Compliance Technique
narratives.description: Security posture management technique for OpenShift platforms

narrativeContexts.context: OpenShift security posture evolves from initial assessment through foundational identity controls, shift-left pipeline integration, automated governance, to adaptive security, following the IDP Essentials principle that the secure path should be the easy path.

Begin with Compliance Operator baseline scans and threat landscape assessment, establish foundational identity and secrets management, integrate security controls into CI/CD golden paths, advance to policy-as-code enforcement with supply chain verification, culminating in adaptive security with threat intelligence and zero-trust architecture.
Avoid treating security as post-deployment hardening; integrate controls into platform provisioning and developer golden paths to prevent security friction that drives shadow IT adoption.

narratives.name: Platform Security Hardening Technique
narratives.description: Platform security hardening technique for OpenShift infrastructure

narrativeContexts.context: Platform security hardening progresses alongside platform provisioning, with security controls embedded into architecture selection and baseline configuration phases.

During architecture selection, choose private cluster topology, enable etcd encryption, and plan FIPS compliance. At baseline, integrate OAuth, automate certificate rotation, separate infrastructure nodes, and remove default admin accounts.
Avoid deferring security hardening to post-provisioning; etcd encryption and FIPS mode must be enabled during installation and cannot be retroactively applied.

citationNames: OpenShift Security Best Practices for Kubernetes Cluster Design

narratives.name: Security & Compliance Overview
narratives.description: PDCA continuous improvement cycle for platform security posture management

narrativeContexts.context: Security architecture begins with assessing threat landscape, regulatory requirements, and organizational risk tolerance, establishing baseline controls and zero-trust principles aligned to the IDP Essentials security posture model.

Implementation progresses through layered defenses: foundational identity and secrets management, shift-left pipeline integration, network isolation via policies, runtime protection via SCCs and mesh encryption, and supply chain integrity via cryptographic signing.

Continuous verification ensures security posture through automated compliance scanning, policy-as-code enforcement, signature validation, and audit logging aligned to regulatory frameworks and CNCF maturity assessment.

Refinement closes gaps identified through security reviews, advancing toward adaptive security with ambient mesh, post-quantum cryptography, zero-trust architecture, and threat-intelligence-driven policy evolution.

activities.name: Assess Security Posture
activities.description: Assess current platform security posture against threat landscape and compliance requirements.

narratives.name: Assess Security Posture Technique

narrativeContexts.context: Security posture assessment establishes the baseline understanding of risks, compliance gaps, and threat vectors specific to the OpenShift container platform environment.

Conduct threat landscape analysis for container platform risks including container breakout, lateral movement, and supply chain compromise. Map regulatory requirements (FIPS, STIGs, CIS Kubernetes) to OpenShift capabilities. Run initial Compliance Operator scans against CIS benchmarks. Document security control gaps and prioritize remediation based on risk severity.
Avoid treating security assessment as a one-time activity; establish baseline metrics that enable continuous posture tracking and trend analysis.

activities.name: Establish Foundational Security Controls
activities.description: Implement core identity, access control, and secrets management as foundational security.

narratives.name: Foundational Security Controls Technique
narratives.description: Technique for establishing foundational security controls

narrativeContexts.context: Foundational security controls establish the P0 security priorities: identity management, access control, secrets management, and encryption that must be in place before shift-left practices.

Integrate OAuth with enterprise identity provider and remove kube-admin account. Configure RBAC policies for least-privilege access. Enable etcd encryption at rest with key rotation. Deploy centralized secrets management. Configure private cluster topology with bastion host access.
Do not skip foundational controls to rush to advanced capabilities; identity and access management gaps undermine all subsequent security layers.

citationNames: OpenShift Security Best Practices for Kubernetes Cluster Design

activities.name: Implement Security Network Policies
activities.description: Define NetworkPolicy resources to restrict pod-to-pod traffic with deny-by-default posture.

narratives.name: Network Policy Implementation Technique
narratives.description: Technique for implementing deny-by-default network policies

narrativeContexts.context: OpenShift networking defaults to allowing all pod-to-pod communication, creating a large attack surface if a pod is compromised. NetworkPolicy resources restrict traffic to only required flows, embodying zero-trust networking principles.

Begin by understanding application communication requirements through traffic analysis or architecture documentation. Start with deny-by-default baseline by creating NetworkPolicy with empty ingress array, then create additive policies permitting specific flows using label selectors. Always permit DNS traffic to kube-dns on port 53.

Test policies in non-production before applying to production, as overly restrictive rules can break applications. Monitor NetworkPolicy behavior using flow logs and document policies alongside deployment manifests in Git for GitOps workflows.

citationNames: OpenShift Networking and Cluster Access Best Practices

activities.name: Deploy Service Mesh for mTLS
activities.description: Deploy OpenShift Service Mesh (Istio) to enforce mutual TLS for service communication.

narratives.name: Service Mesh Deployment Technique
narratives.description: Technique for deploying service mesh with mutual TLS

narrativeContexts.context: OpenShift Service Mesh provides mutual TLS encryption and identity-based authorization for microservices communication, advancing beyond network-layer segmentation to application-layer security.

Install OpenShift Service Mesh operator and create ServiceMeshControlPlane. Enable automatic sidecar injection. Configure PeerAuthentication for strict mutual TLS. Define AuthorizationPolicy resources. Use Kiali for service topology visualization.
Service mesh introduces performance overhead from sidecar proxies; monitor resource usage and consider ambient mode. Ensure certificate rotation is automated to prevent expiration-related outages.

citationNames: OpenShift Networking and Cluster Access Best Practices

activities.name: Configure Security Context Constraints
activities.description: Configure and enforce SCCs to restrict container privileges and capabilities.

narratives.name: SCC Configuration Technique
narratives.description: Technique for configuring Security Context Constraints

narrativeContexts.context: Security Context Constraints prevent privilege escalation and limit container capabilities by enforcing policies on pod security settings, ensuring containers run with minimal privileges.

Use restricted SCC as default for all applications. Review application requirements to determine if restricted SCC is sufficient. Document SCC exceptions with security review and approval process. Audit service account to SCC bindings regularly.
Applications expecting to run as root will fail under restricted SCC; modify applications to support arbitrary UID rather than granting privileged access.

activities.name: Implement Cryptographic Image Signing
activities.description: Deploy Trusted Artifact Signer and configure ImagePolicy for signature verification.

narratives.name: Image Signing Technique
narratives.description: Technique for implementing cryptographic image signing

narrativeContexts.context: Cryptographic signing with Sigstore ensures only verified, attested artifacts are deployed, protecting against supply chain attacks by validating artifact provenance and integrity.

Deploy Trusted Artifact Signer operator. Configure CI/CD pipelines to sign images and generate SBOM and provenance attestations. Store signatures in Rekor transparency log. Define ImagePolicy resources. Configure admission webhook to validate signatures before pod creation.
Key management is critical; use hardware security modules or cloud KMS for signing key protection. Ensure Rekor is highly available to prevent deployment outages.

activities.name: Conduct Compliance Scanning
activities.description: Configure Compliance Operator to scan against CIS benchmarks and regulatory requirements.

narratives.name: Compliance Scanning Technique

narrativeContexts.context: Compliance Operator automates security posture assessment against industry benchmarks (CIS Kubernetes, PCI-DSS, NIST), eliminating manual reviews and enabling continuous verification.

Install Compliance Operator from OperatorHub. Create ScanSettingBinding resources specifying compliance profiles. Schedule scans automatically. Review ComplianceCheckResult objects. Apply ComplianceRemediation resources. Export reports for audit.
Not all compliance checks can be automatically remediated; manual review and risk acceptance processes are required for exceptions.

narratives.name: Build-Time Security Technique
narratives.description: Technique for integrating build-time security controls

narrativeContexts.context: Build-time security shifts vulnerability detection left by integrating scanning gates and multi-stage builds into CI/CD pipelines.

Implement multi-stage Dockerfiles separating build and runtime. Configure vulnerability scanning to fail builds exceeding severity threshold. Integrate image signing with Trusted Artifact Signer. Generate SBOM during build.
Overly strict scanning gates can block legitimate deployments; establish severity thresholds and exception workflows balancing security with velocity.

citationNames: 14 Best Practices for Developing Applications on OpenShift

patterns.name: Security Maturity Lifecycle
patterns.description: Progressive security posture enhancement from assessment through adaptive security using PDCA improvement.

patternViews.name: Security Assessment
patternViews.description: Assess security posture and identify compliance gaps.

narrativeContexts.context: Security maturity begins with assessing current posture, identifying gaps against regulatory requirements and CIS benchmarks, establishing baseline image security controls, and planning network isolation strategy.

patternViews.name: Foundational Controls
patternViews.description: Establish identity, access, and secrets management.

narrativeContexts.context: Foundational security establishes P0 priorities: SSO with MFA, least-privilege RBAC, centralized secrets management, etcd encryption, and private cluster configuration as prerequisites for shift-left practices.

patternViews.name: Shift-Left Security
patternViews.description: Embed security controls into pipelines and runtime.

narrativeContexts.context: Security controls are operationalized through build-time scanning gates, deny-by-default NetworkPolicies, service mesh mutual TLS, and SCC enforcement, shifting security left into development and delivery pipelines.

patternViews.name: Automated Governance
patternViews.description: Automate supply chain security and policy enforcement.

narrativeContexts.context: Automated governance verifies artifact integrity through SBOM generation, Sigstore signing, ImagePolicy admission validation, and continuous compliance scanning with policy-as-code enforcement.

patternViews.name: Adaptive Security
patternViews.description: Achieve adaptive zero-trust with continuous evolution.

narrativeContexts.context: Adaptive security achieved through ambient mesh eliminating sidecar overhead, Zero Trust Workload Identity federating identities, post-quantum cryptography, threat-intelligence-driven policy evolution, and continuous compliance automation.
